newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Chemapol plans Czech rights issue, delays GDRs.
newsitem.headline: Chemapol plans Czech rights issue, delays GDRs.

text.p: The rapidly-growing Czech chemicals and industrial conglomerate Chemapol Group a.s. said on Friday that it planned to launch a domestic rights issue to expand equity by 500 million to 800 million crowns.

Acting spokeswoman Jirina Calfova told Reuters that the rights issue would be put to a vote at an extraordinary general meeting in late October, and that a previously planned global depositary receipt (GDR) issue of a minimum 600 million crowns would be put to a later shareholders' meeting in early 1997.
She said that a general meeting planned for today was delayed until October 25 because heavy domestic interest in new Chemapol Group shares caused management to rethink its plans.
"The main reason was continuing strong interest from current shareholders and domestic investors to get shares of our company, and therefore we preferred a domestic issue," Calfova said.

She said the domestic issue would be structured in two rounds with unsubscribed shares carried over as a public offering in a second round. Cheampol Group's current basic equity totals 1.68 billion crowns.

Calfova, who serves as board secretary, said the closely-held company has applied for its first listing on the Prague Stock Exchange. The initial listing would be on the bourse's so-called free market, not its main market.

Shares in the group -- which controlled, at last count in August, 67 chemical, industrial, trading and media companies -- last traded on Thursday at 2,300 crowns, up 44 crowns on the over-the-counter Czech RM-System where liquidity is negligible.
The company's original plan to issue GDRs, announced in August, was to be arranged by the investment bank HSBC and Chemapol's own finance unit Expandia Finance.

"Another reason...to delay the GDR issue... is organisation changes with regards to our acquisitions, and our transformation into a sub-holding structure in order to become more transparent abroad," Calfova said.

Chemapol has grown from mostly oil trading company -- a business it was partially pushed out of by local refineries -- to control an estimated 20 billion crowns in equity throughout its vast holdings.
The group reported consolidated unaudited net profit for the first half of this year of 290 million crowns.
The group posted audited net profit of 62.5 million crowns in 1995. It had total sales of over 40 billion crowns in 1995 and 29 billion crowns in the first half of 1996.
